sections.title: Just Shashwat, Outside Work
sections.content:
This part of the profile is not about job titles, resumes, or professional achievements. This is simply about Shashwat as a person, outside work and outside structured expectations.

Shashwat is naturally curious and reflective. He enjoys building things and thinking deeply, but he also values slowing down, exploring random interests, and spending time on things that don’t have a clear objective or measurable outcome. He believes that not everything needs to be optimized — some things are worth doing simply because they feel good or interesting.

This profile exists for people who are casually exploring the website or are curious about the person behind the systems. It’s meant to feel relaxed, human, and unfiltered — more like a conversation than a presentation.

sections.title: Creativity, Painting & Art
sections.content:
Shashwat has always had a creative side beyond technology. He used to paint regularly and has worked on wall paintings at different points in his life. Painting has been one of the ways he expressed himself creatively, especially during phases when he wanted to disconnect from screens and logic-heavy thinking.

Wall painting, in particular, taught him patience and comfort with imperfection. Unlike code, a brush stroke cannot be undone easily, and that forces a different kind of mindset — one that accepts mistakes and adapts creatively. Even though he doesn’t paint as frequently now, that creative instinct still influences how he thinks about design, visuals, and storytelling.

For Shashwat, creative hobbies are not about mastery or productivity. They are about balance, expression, and doing something purely for the joy of it.

sections.title: Curiosity, Learning & Space Fascination
sections.content:
Shashwat is deeply curious by nature. He enjoys reading about new technologies, emerging ideas, and concepts that expand how he understands the world. His curiosity is not limited to what is immediately useful — he often explores topics simply because they sound interesting.

One area that consistently fascinates him is space. He enjoys reading about space missions, black holes, astrophysics concepts, and future exploration efforts. For him, space represents scale, mystery, and perspective. Learning about it reminds him how small individual problems are in the context of the universe.

Much of his learning is unstructured. He often goes down random rabbit holes without a predefined goal, driven purely by curiosity and the desire to be amazed rather than to extract immediate value.

sections.title: Movies, Shows & Good Stories
sections.content:
Shashwat enjoys watching movies and TV shows, especially those with strong storytelling and well-developed characters. His favorite genres are science fiction and mystery — stories that make you think, question reality, or slowly reveal deeper layers over time.

Shows like *Suits* and *Breaking Bad* are among the ones he has enjoyed the most. He appreciates narratives that explore complex characters, long-term arcs, and moral gray areas rather than relying purely on fast-paced action.

For him, good stories are another form of exploration. They offer a way to step into different worlds, perspectives, and mindsets, even if just for a few hours.

sections.title: Sports, Games & Physical Activity
sections.content:
Sports have played a role in Shashwat’s life at different stages. During his childhood, he played a lot of cricket, mostly for fun rather than competition. Those early experiences were about enjoying the game, being outdoors, and staying active.

In college, he picked up squash and grew to enjoy its fast-paced and mentally engaging nature. Squash combines physical endurance with strategy and focus, which made it particularly appealing during academically intense periods.

Even though he is not actively playing competitive sports now, Shashwat values the mindset sports cultivate — resilience, focus, and the ability to stay calm under pressure.

sections.title: Poker, Strategy & Hostel Nights
sections.content:
Shashwat is a big fan of poker. During his college years, poker nights in the hostel were a regular and memorable part of life. These sessions were less about money and more about strategy, psychology, and decision-making under uncertainty.

Poker appealed to him because of its blend of probability, risk management, and human behavior. It teaches that even correct decisions can sometimes lead to losses, and that emotional control is just as important as technical skill.

Those late-night poker games remain some of his favorite college memories — filled with debates, laughter, overthinking simple hands, and learning how people think under pressure.

sections.title: Music, Mood & Everyday Vibes
sections.content:
Shashwat listens to a wide mix of music genres, though he tends to enjoy pop music the most. For him, music is less about deep analysis and more about setting a mood or background energy.

Music often plays alongside whatever he is doing — thinking, relaxing, traveling, or just spending time alone. He doesn’t restrict himself to specific genres; if a song feels right, he listens to it.

Rather than demanding attention, music acts as a steady presence that helps shape his environment and state of mind.

sections.title: Mountains, Travel & the Love for the Road
sections.content:
Shashwat has a deep and personal connection with mountains. He grew up around them — he is from Jammu — and has seen mountains throughout his life. Because of that, mountains don’t feel like a vacation destination to him; they feel familiar and grounding.

He genuinely enjoys hiking and trekking, especially challenging trails that test both physical endurance and mental resilience. Over the years, he has been on treks such as the Serpahs trek and the Great Lakes trek, experiences that reinforced his love for long walks, thin air, quiet landscapes, and earning every view.

Travel, for Shashwat, is more about experience than luxury. He enjoys traveling with people, planning trips, and exploring new places. He has traveled extensively across India, from Jammu and Kashmir all the way down to Kerala, and each journey has added a new perspective.

While he also enjoys beaches, he will always be more of a mountain person than a beach person. Mountains give him calm, perspective, and a sense of reset that very few other environments do.

If someone wants to plan a trip, go trekking, or explore somewhere new, Shashwat is almost always in. Traveling — especially to the mountains — is one of the things that genuinely excites and energizes him.

sections.title: IIT Delhi — A Chapter That Shaped Him
sections.content:
Shashwat studied at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi, where he pursued Mathematics and Computing. But for him, IIT Delhi was never just about a degree or a branch — it was a phase of life that shaped how he thinks, learns, and sees the world.

The Mathematics and Computing program was intense, demanding, and intellectually stimulating. Being surrounded by extremely sharp, competitive, and curious peers created an environment where learning happened constantly — not just in classrooms, but in hostels, late-night discussions, and casual conversations. Everyone around him was good at something, and that pushed him to explore many different dimensions of himself.

One of the most meaningful parts of his time at IIT Delhi was the people. He met some incredibly intelligent, driven, and thoughtful individuals, many of whom became close friends and some of the best people he knows today. Hostel life played a huge role in this — shared rooms, late-night talks, random plans, exams, celebrations, failures, and small everyday moments that slowly turn strangers into lifelong friends.

College life gave him some of his happiest moments — spontaneous trips, endless conversations, inside jokes, late-night games, and the freedom to explore interests without knowing exactly where they would lead. At the same time, it also brought some of the most challenging moments — academic pressure, self-doubt, difficult phases, and the constant need to grow and adapt in a highly competitive environment.

Those challenges were just as important as the good times. They taught him resilience, humility, and how to handle uncertainty. Being in such an intense and intellectually charged space helped him understand his own limits, push past them, and become more comfortable with discomfort.

Looking back, Shashwat sees IIT Delhi as much more than an academic institution. It was a place where he learned from people as much as from books, where friendships shaped his worldview, and where some of the most defining memories of his life were created. It was a chapter filled with growth, struggle, joy, and learning — one that continues to influence who he is today.
